issue_context.summary: A Store installation of PowerToys shows an unexplained shortcut conflict associated with Keyboard Manager and Advanced Paste. A new commenter suggests Win+Shift+Q, but the author has not confirmed the key or provided the data needed to isolate registration versus display attribution.
known_information: The issue is open and labeled Issue-Bug, Needs-Author-Feedback, Needs-Triage, and Product-General.
The reporter supplied PowerToys 0.101.2362, Windows 11 build 26200, per-user/non-elevated execution, three screenshots, and a diagnostic ZIP link.
The reporter says the conflict window shows a shortcut not tied to a visible function, associated with Keyboard Manager, and redirected to Advanced Paste.
The issue author says they do not know how the shortcut appeared and provides no reproduction steps.
The automated triage comment says the supplied archive was rejected because of an oversized entry and could not be analyzed.
A community commenter wrote that Win+Shift+Q opens Keyboard Manager; this is an unverified lead, not author-confirmed issue evidence.
The current conflict UI resolves conflict groups through ShortcutConflictViewModel.ProcessConflicts, SetupModuleData, and GetHotkeyLocalizationHeader.
HotkeyConflictIgnoreHelper persists ignored shortcut tuples and is consulted by both the dashboard and conflict window.
inferences: If the author confirms Win+Shift+Q, the report can be compared against the exact conflict tuple and the module/action accessor IDs instead of relying on screenshot interpretation.

The Keyboard Manager versus Advanced Paste wording may be incorrect attribution of a conflict payload, but it could also reflect two real registrations; the current evidence does not choose between them.
The rejected archive means current conflict-detector logs and persisted ignore state cannot yet be compared with the displayed row.
issue_context.analysis: The new comment reduces the search space but is not enough to change the author-evidence gate. The current source shows separate stages for conflict-group processing, module/action lookup, Advanced Paste custom-action header localization, and ignored-shortcut filtering. Exact shortcut text, action IDs, and a repeatable sequence are therefore the minimum evidence needed to decide whether a code change belongs in conflict detection, settings mapping, or persisted ignore handling.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and both public comments, including the original automated triage request and the new Win+Shift+Q observation.

Reviewed src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/ViewModels/ShortcutConflictViewModel.cs: ProcessConflicts builds HotkeySettings from the conflict tuple, SetupModuleData resolves module settings and hotkey accessors, and GetHotkeyLocalizationHeader has a special Advanced Paste custom-action path.
Reviewed src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/Helpers/HotkeyConflictIgnoreHelper.cs: ignored shortcuts are persisted in GeneralSettings and compared by modifier flags plus key code.
Compared #50239 (false-positive Win+Shift+C system conflict), #49423, #43665, and #37085. They are related conflict-detection reports but none is confirmed as a duplicate of #50402.

Reviewed public conflict-window history associated with PRs #41029, #41729, and #42440. Those changes introduced conflict detection, ignored-conflict handling, and singleton-window behavior; no existing fix attempt covers this exact report.

comment.body: Thanks for the screenshots and for reporting this on PowerToys 0.101.2362. A commenter has suggested Win+Shift+Q, but please confirm whether that is the exact shortcut shown in your conflict row and include the exact Keyboard Manager and Advanced Paste action names displayed there. Please also provide numbered steps from opening PowerToys to seeing the row, and say whether it remains after restarting PowerToys. The original ZIP could not be analyzed because of an oversized entry, so immediately after reproducing the confirmed conflict, add a comment containing `/bugreport` and attach the newly generated ZIP. These details will distinguish a real registration conflict from stale data or incorrect module/action attribution.
